title: Residential Property Seller Disclosure Statement
description: Iowa Code §558A.1 et seq. requires sellers of residential real property (1-4 units including manufactured homes on permanent foundations) to deliver a written disclosure statement to the buyer. The disclosure covers structural, mechanical, environmental conditions, and known defects. Must be delivered before acceptance of the offer. Seller must update if conditions change before closing.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered before acceptance. Buyer may rescind within 72 hours of receipt if not previously provided. Exemptions for foreclosures, estate sales, and new construction (Iowa Code §558A.2).

title: Agency Disclosure Requirements
description: Iowa Administrative Code 193E-12 and Iowa Code §543B.56A require licensees to provide written agency disclosure at the first substantial contact. Iowa recognizes buyer's agents, seller's agents, dual agents (with written consent), and designated agents within the same brokerage. Written informed consent is required for dual agency.

required_actions.note: Written disclosure required at first substantial contact. Dual agency requires written informed consent from both parties.

title: Attorney or Title Company Closing
description: Iowa is unique in that it has no title insurance industry by historical practice. Closings are typically handled by attorneys who provide title opinions (abstract and opinion). Iowa Code §16.91 governs title guaranty through the Iowa Finance Authority's Title Guaranty Division, which provides a state-run title guaranty program as an alternative to commercial title insurance.

required_actions.note: Iowa uses attorney-prepared title opinions based on abstracts, or Iowa Title Guaranty certificates. No commercial title insurance companies operate in Iowa. The Iowa Finance Authority Title Guaranty Division provides the title guaranty product.

metadata.note: Iowa is the only US state that effectively prohibits commercial title insurance.

title: Radon Disclosure and Testing
description: Iowa Code §558A.4(3) specifically requires sellers to disclose known radon hazards on the property disclosure form. Iowa has some of the highest average indoor radon levels in the United States. The Iowa Department of Public Health maintains radon zone data. Sellers must disclose known test results and any radon mitigation systems.

required_actions.note: Seller must disclose known radon test results and mitigation systems on statutory disclosure form. Iowa average indoor radon is ~8.5 pCi/L (over 2x the EPA action level).
EPA recommends mitigation for levels above 4.0 pCi/L.

title: Groundwater Hazard Statement
description: Iowa Code §558.69 requires the seller to deliver a completed Groundwater Hazard Statement to the buyer before transfer. The statement discloses whether the property contains or has contained underground storage tanks, hazardous waste, private burial sites, wells (active, abandoned, or sealed), and solid waste disposal sites. This is a separate requirement from the general property disclosure.

required_actions.note: Separate from the general property disclosure. Must be delivered before transfer. Covers underground tanks, hazardous waste, wells, burial sites, and solid waste.
